jobs.title: Vice-President, Finance and Operations
jobs.description:
The University of British Columbia (UBC) is one of the world’s leading research universities—an institution inspiring people, ideas and actions for a better world. With two main campuses in Vancouver and the Okanagan, more than 73,000 students, over 20,000 faculty and staff, 25,000 full-time campus residents, over 435,000 alumni, and an annual consolidated budget over $4 billion, UBC combines global reach with a deep commitment to Canada, British Columbia and the communities it serves.

UBC’s academic excellence and societal impact are driven by a research community attracting close to $1 billion in annual funding, and supported by extraordinary assets including extensive physical infrastructure, a $3.5 billion endowment fund, and a full range of services that sustain vibrant learning, working and living environments. UBC’s Strategic Directions 2025–2030set an ambitious course for discovery, partnership, emerging technologies and collaboration across its two distinct and complementary campuses, and reaffirms UBC’s long-standing commitments to reconciliation, inclusion and sustainability.

UBC is seeking a strategic and collaborative Vice-President, Finance and Operations to align financial and operational capacity with its academic and research ambitions. The VPFO will provide integrated leadership for financial strategy and stewardship, financial planning and analysis, treasury, financial operations, facilities and infrastructure, capital investment, safety, risk and assurance, while supporting the long-term value of the university’s physical and financial assets. This is a significant opportunity to help shape the future successes of one of the leading research institutions in Canada and globally.

A trusted partner to the entire UBC Community - including the President and executive team, Board of Governors, Host Nations, Deans and senior leaders, student leaders, campus residents and alumni community - the VPFO will translate institutional priorities into sustainable multi-year financial and operating strategies in service of the University’s academic mission. Working collegially across faculties, campuses and administrative units, the Vice-President will strengthen planning, resource allocation and risk-informed decision-making, and lead modernization of systems, processes and services. The role calls for a leader who builds and engages strong teams, communicates complex choices clearly, has successfully demonstrated change in a complex environment, and balances institutional consistency with the needs of a distributed academic environment.

The ideal candidate brings executive-level experience with responsibility for finance and significant operational functions in an organization of comparable scale, complexity and public accountability. Experience in a large Canadian research-intensive university is strongly preferred; leaders from other highly complex sectors will also be considered. Candidates will demonstrate strategic financial depth, operational breadth, sound governance and a track record of leading enterprise-wide change with integrity and transparency. A sustained commitment to reconciliation, inclusion and sustainability is essential. A university degree is required; a relevant graduate degree, CPA designation, or other relevant financial designations are highly desirable. A combination of equivalent senior leadership experience and education credentials will be considered.

To explore this exceptional opportunity further, please contact our Search Consultants at Boyden at ubc@boyden.com or click Apply to submit your resume.

At UBC, we believe that a diverse workforce contributes to the pursuit of excellence in research, innovation, and learning. We encourage applications from marginalized groups based on the grounds enumerated under the B.C. Human Rights Code. All applicants will be asked to complete a confidential diversity survey. If you have any accommodation or accessibility needs during the job application process, please contact the Centre for Workplace Accessibility at workplace.accessibility@ubc.ca.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. We thank all applicants for their interest in this position. Please note that we will only be in contact with those individuals moving forward within this search. In accordance with BC’s Pay Transparency Act, the position has an expected base salary range of $340,000 - $380,000.

jobs.description:
About Us

Mayfair is a private family office. We design, build and run the office that sits around a principal’s wealth and their life, so the people who created that wealth don’t have to run it themselves.

The people who join now will shape what Mayfair becomes, from how we bring on new principals to how we work together. Your work will show up in the company as much as in the principals you serve.

The Role

You’ll run the office for each principal you serve. You’ll be their single point of contact and direct the work across our five verticals. You’ll sit beside the principal, not three layers below them, and see the whole picture rather than one slice of it. Your judgment shapes real outcomes for the people we serve. You’ll work with a small number of principals. How many depends on the level of service each one has chosen. You become the person they call first. When something needs a decision, you bring it to them with the work done and the options framed. The decisions stay with them.

You won’t carry the work alone. Our own people run the five verticals behind you, and AI handles much of the research, reporting, and document prep underneath. That leaves your time for the principal and the judgment calls.

You don’t need to be an expert in all matters. You need to know when a question calls for a specialist, bring in the right people, and make sure the principal has what they need to decide. Knowing who to call matters more than knowing every answer.

What You'll Do

• Become the principal’s right hand, and build the relationship over years, not quarters.
• Run the reporting and meeting cadence so the principal knows what’s coming before it arrives.
• Keep the decision log. When something needs a decision, bring it with the work done and the options framed.
• Have the difficult conversations when they come up, whether that’s telling a principal a plan won’t work, holding an advisor to a missed deadline, or helping family members work through a disagreement.
• Direct our Asset Administration & Reporting, Banking & Treasury, Financial Operations, Wealth Oversight and Tax & Structures teams so the work gets done well and on time. In a given month that might mean signing off the bill pay schedule, approving a capital call, reviewing the monthly close and cash forecast, or planning the tax work ahead of a business sale.
• Oversee the life side of the office: property managers, household staff, aviation, travel, IT and security.
• Put governance and controls in place, from approval limits to how payments are authorized, and keep them working.
• Hold the principal’s lawyers, accountants, bankers and investment managers accountable to one plan and one set of facts.
• Spot early when a situation needs a specialist. You don’t need to be the expert, but you need to know when one is needed. If a principal is heading toward a sale, the tax and legal team should be in place months before the deal, not the week it closes.
• Lead triage for new principals: map every advisor, account, entity and asset, learn the principal’s values, and set up how they want approvals to work.
• Help shape how Mayfair onboards, reports and runs reviews as the company grows.

What We're Looking For

• Five or more years at manager or senior manager level in a Big Four private client group, or a comparable role in private banking, wealth advisory or a multi-family office, including leading complex, multi-advisor projects for ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families.
• Strong emotional intelligence. You read people well and earn trust quickly. You notice what a principal isn’t saying, stay steady when a conversation gets difficult, and can tell them something they don’t want to hear. This matters more than anything else on this list.
• Ease with significant wealth. You’re comfortable with founders, executives and multi-generational families, and you hold your own with them and with their lawyer, accountant and banker in the same room.
• A generalist’s curiosity. One week it’s a pre-sale reorganization, the next it’s an aircraft purchase, a new trust or a renovation. You don’t need to be the expert in each. What matters is learning enough to run it and knowing when to bring in someone who is.
• Clear, simple communication. You can take something complex and make it simple. A principal should be able to read your summary in five minutes and know the options, the trade-offs and what needs deciding.
• A CPA, TEP, CFA or equivalent professional designation.
• Flexibility to work across North American time zones. Some travel is required, in Canada and the US.
• You live in Canada and are legally entitled to work in Canada.

Nice to Have

• Experience at an early startup, ideally one still defining its own operating model while building.
• Background in wealth tech, legal tech, or fintech.
• Working familiarity with family office concepts: trusts, entity structures, investment policy statements, manager oversight, and how those pieces interact.
• Experience working alongside a small team without a large product organization or established tooling around you.
• A CPA In-Depth or Master of Taxation, Canada and US cross-border experience, or time in a family office.

Logistics

• Remote, based anywhere in Canada. Full-time and permanent.
• Base salary range: $165,000 to $185,000 CAD per year. Where you land in the range reflects your experience.
• Standard business hours, with flexibility across North American time zones.
• Some travel is required, in Canada and the US.

How We Hire

Five values guide how we work:
Do What Is Right.
Be In The Arena.
Earn The Right.
All In. One Team.
Fear Nothing. Solve Everything.
They are the first filter for anyone who joins us, ahead of the interview and ahead of skills.

Because this role approves client payments and other financial transactions, the process includes a background check, including a credit check, with your written consent.

We give everyone we interview an answer.

How to Apply

Apply through LinkedIn with your resume. We highly recommend a cover letter. Make it the first page of the same PDF you upload as your resume.

In the first line of your cover letter, tell us your favourite restaurant, or a place you would take a visitor, in the city where you live.

About Coursera + Udemy

Coursera and Udemy are now one company, bringing together two mission-driven brands to create the world’s most powerful platform for turning learning into progress. Together, we help more than 300 million learners and 12,000+ enterprise customers build the skills they need for a world being reshaped by AI. Read more about the combined company by visiting our blog.

Why join us now?

AI is transforming how people learn, work, and grow, and the need for new skills has never been greater. Coursera brings trusted content and credentials from leading university and industry partners, while Udemy brings a dynamic skills marketplace and global network of real-world experts. By combining these strengths, we can connect more people and organizations to the skills they need, when they need them.

Shape What Comes Next

By joining our team, you’ll have the opportunity to reshape how the world learns and applies skills—and help millions of people participate in the new economy. Bring your ideas, expertise, and perspective to meaningful work that can make a difference at global scale.

How We Work

Coursera + Udemy lets you choose the best way to work, whether it’s from home, an office, or a collaboration space. We’re a globally distributed team that comes together intentionally for collaboration, complex problem-solving, and key milestones — creating opportunities for teams to come together. If you’re ready to make a global impact, help scale unique products across Coursera + Udemy, and grow your career, apply below.

Job Overview:

Within Professional Services, you'll lead the Solutions Architecture team through a fundamental change: from a technical intake team that passes integration work to third parties to a team that designs and builds the integrations we choose to own on Workato. You'll decide which integrations are strategic to own and which third parties can deliver faster, and you'll balance capacity across Coursera and Udemy technical work. You'll lay a foundation to build from, so that integrations are productized and reusable rather than one-offs, and you'll upskill the team to design, build, and test the way an engineering team does. You'll also take ownership of integrations built by third parties for both Coursera and Udemy, and decide what, if anything, to migrate in house. This is a highly operational role. You'll redesign how the team works with Product, Partnerships, Presales, and Customer Support, define workflows that are not yet defined, and build the delivery discipline, capacity model, and metrics that make the function run like a well-oiled machine. You'll report to the Senior Director of Professional Services and partner closely with the Director of AI Innovation to streamline how the team works.

General Description

The Director of Financial Resilience is a new position, created to launch and lead a department and team that assists domestic violence survivors in achieving financial stability, safety, and long-term wealth growth. This position will guide a team of three financial coaches, shape trauma-informed programming, and build partnerships with financial institutions and community organizations that expand access to resources for survivors. The Director will create a new department that will integrate a financial resilience model across New Destiny’s housing programs, with the goal of increasing the number of domestic violence survivors able to receive financial stabilization services, deepen survivors’ financial literacy and knowledge, and grow survivors’ financial health and wellness for long-term stability. This work is rooted in trauma-informed care and tailored to the experience and needs of the formerly homeless domestic violence survivors we serve.

Design, implement, and evaluate financial empowerment programs, including coaching, credit repair, savings programs, asset building, debt management, and banking access.

Develop key performance indicators to track outcomes and report to leadership and funders.

Provide access to training to financial coaches, including best practices and recovery from financial abuse.

Partner with community organizations focusing on income security, financial independence and growth, including legal partners, eviction-prevention organizations, workforce development opportunities, and other social services to create seamless referral pathways.
Identify and pursue opportunities for matched savings and other wealth-building initiatives.

About Bu

Since 1981, Baragar Systems has partnered with K–12 school districts across Canada and the United States to provide data-driven planning tools that transform complex enrolment, boundary, staffing, and demographic data into clear, confident decisions. Serving more than 100 school districts, Baragar has built a reputation for deep educational planning expertise and meaningful impact on how education leaders plan for the future. Our product suite includes Demographic Dynamics (enrolment forecasting), GeoSchool (boundary planning and analysis), ThemeMap (geographic data visualization), District Intelligence (data dashboards and reporting), Staff Allocator, School Locator and School Boundaries Online. All tools purpose-built for the unique planning challenges school districts face. Baragar has historically operated as a service-first organization. Each year, the team delivers custom geospatial and demographic data packages, assembled by experienced data analysts and GIS specialists, alongside an annual software deliverable. Deep client engagement, hands-on support, and tailored training are central to how Baragar works. This model has created strong, trust-based relationships, and that expertise remains a core part of who we are.

Baragar operates as a focused business unit within Univerus, combining the intimacy and expertise of a specialist team with the scale and investment of a growing global organization.

Learn more at baragar.com

Position Details

Hours: 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday

Salary Range: $120,000 to $145,000 CAD per year

Location: Surrey, BC, Canada - Hybrid

This is a replacement position.

Role Overview

Baragar is entering a new chapter, one that builds on decades of service excellence while developing stronger internal accountability for its technology and product direction. The domain expertise, client relationships, and delivery capability that define Baragar today are what we’re building from, and what we’re committed to protecting as we grow. We are now establishing clearer in-house leadership over product direction, a more deliberate approach to technology decision-making, and the capacity to develop internal technical capability alongside our existing development partnerships.

We are seeking a Director, Technology & Product to lead that work. This is a senior role spanning five core areas: leading change, technology leadership and modernization, product and delivery management, building internal capability, and budget and governance. The successful candidate will hold both the strategic and the operational; someone who understands legacy systems, manages vendor and delivery relationships with confidence, brings clear technology judgment, and has the presence and discipline to drive meaningful change in an organization with a long operational history. This is a role focused on forward momentum, building on what works while creating the conditions for meaningful change. It is not a purely strategic role; the person who succeeds here will be equally comfortable doing the work as directing it: writing requirements, staying close to delivery, and investing the time to deeply understand Baragar’s domain, its data, and how the organization operates before

driving change. They will have a direct hand in shaping what Baragar’s technology foundation looks like over the next several years. The expectation, and the commitment from the organization, is that this investment of time and understanding comes first.

Organizational Relationship

This role reports directly to the EVP of Baragar Systems and operates as the senior internal technology voice for the business unit. The Director, Technology & Product works closely with external development partners who currently deliver all of the product work, as well as with Baragar’s data analysts, GIS specialists, and client-facing staff. Univerus technical leadership on strategic alignment and collaborate with counterparts in other business units.

Leading Change

Act as the senior internal technology voice in leadership discussions, vendor discussions, and strategic planning, bringing clarity and confidence to complex technical decisions.
Hold the organization accountable to transformation milestones, engaging teams and leadership with clarity and credibility, while respecting the expertise and customer value already built into the business.
Communicate technology direction, progress, and change clearly across the broader organization ensuring parties at all levels understand the why, not just the what.

Technology Leadership & Modernization

Lead the planning, resourcing, timelines, and delivery across multiple software products.
Oversee backlog management, release planning, and production support.

Partner with staff at all levels to translate organizational needs into clear technical priorities.
Translate between stakeholder requirements and technical constraints, turning business needs into clear development requirements and technical trade-offs into decisions leadership can act on.

transfer and grow over time.

new_jobs.description:
About Us

Mayfair is a private family office. We design, build and run the office that sits around a principal’s wealth and their life, so the people who created that wealth don’t have to run it themselves.

The people who join now will shape what Mayfair becomes, from how we bring on new principals to how we work together. Your work will show up in the company as much as in the principals you serve.

The Role

You’ll run the office for each principal you serve. You’ll be their single point of contact and direct the work across our five verticals. You’ll sit beside the principal, not three layers below them, and see the whole picture rather than one slice of it. Your judgment shapes real outcomes for the people we serve. You’ll work with a small number of principals. How many depends on the level of service each one has chosen. You become the person they call first. When something needs a decision, you bring it to them with the work done and the options framed. The decisions stay with them.

You won’t carry the work alone. Our own people run the five verticals behind you, and AI handles much of the research, reporting, and document prep underneath. That leaves your time for the principal and the judgment calls.

You don’t need to be an expert in all matters. You need to know when a question calls for a specialist, bring in the right people, and make sure the principal has what they need to decide. Knowing who to call matters more than knowing every answer.

What You'll Do

• Become the principal’s right hand, and build the relationship over years, not quarters.
• Run the reporting and meeting cadence so the principal knows what’s coming before it arrives.
• Keep the decision log. When something needs a decision, bring it with the work done and the options framed.
• Have the difficult conversations when they come up, whether that’s telling a principal a plan won’t work, holding an advisor to a missed deadline, or helping family members work through a disagreement.
• Direct our Asset Administration & Reporting, Banking & Treasury, Financial Operations, Wealth Oversight and Tax & Structures teams so the work gets done well and on time. In a given month that might mean signing off the bill pay schedule, approving a capital call, reviewing the monthly close and cash forecast, or planning the tax work ahead of a business sale.
• Oversee the life side of the office: property managers, household staff, aviation, travel, IT and security.
• Put governance and controls in place, from approval limits to how payments are authorized, and keep them working.
• Hold the principal’s lawyers, accountants, bankers and investment managers accountable to one plan and one set of facts.
• Spot early when a situation needs a specialist. You don’t need to be the expert, but you need to know when one is needed. If a principal is heading toward a sale, the tax and legal team should be in place months before the deal, not the week it closes.
• Lead triage for new principals: map every advisor, account, entity and asset, learn the principal’s values, and set up how they want approvals to work.
• Help shape how Mayfair onboards, reports and runs reviews as the company grows.

What We're Looking For

• Five or more years at manager or senior manager level in a Big Four private client group, or a comparable role in private banking, wealth advisory or a multi-family office, including leading complex, multi-advisor projects for ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families.
• Strong emotional intelligence. You read people well and earn trust quickly. You notice what a principal isn’t saying, stay steady when a conversation gets difficult, and can tell them something they don’t want to hear. This matters more than anything else on this list.
• Ease with significant wealth. You’re comfortable with founders, executives and multi-generational families, and you hold your own with them and with their lawyer, accountant and banker in the same room.
• A generalist’s curiosity. One week it’s a pre-sale reorganization, the next it’s an aircraft purchase, a new trust or a renovation. You don’t need to be the expert in each. What matters is learning enough to run it and knowing when to bring in someone who is.
• Clear, simple communication. You can take something complex and make it simple. A principal should be able to read your summary in five minutes and know the options, the trade-offs and what needs deciding.
• A CPA, TEP, CFA or equivalent professional designation.
• Flexibility to work across North American time zones. Some travel is required, in Canada and the US.
• You live in Canada and are legally entitled to work in Canada.

Nice to Have

• Experience at an early startup, ideally one still defining its own operating model while building.
• Background in wealth tech, legal tech, or fintech.
• Working familiarity with family office concepts: trusts, entity structures, investment policy statements, manager oversight, and how those pieces interact.
• Experience working alongside a small team without a large product organization or established tooling around you.
• A CPA In-Depth or Master of Taxation, Canada and US cross-border experience, or time in a family office.

Logistics

• Remote, based anywhere in Canada. Full-time and permanent.
• Base salary range: $165,000 to $185,000 CAD per year. Where you land in the range reflects your experience.
• Standard business hours, with flexibility across North American time zones.
• Some travel is required, in Canada and the US.

How We Hire

Five values guide how we work:
Do What Is Right.
Be In The Arena.
Earn The Right.
All In. One Team.
Fear Nothing. Solve Everything.
They are the first filter for anyone who joins us, ahead of the interview and ahead of skills.

Because this role approves client payments and other financial transactions, the process includes a background check, including a credit check, with your written consent.

We give everyone we interview an answer.

Apply through LinkedIn with your resume. We highly recommend a cover letter. Make it the first page of the same PDF you upload as your resume.

In the first line of your cover letter, tell us your favourite restaurant, or a place you would take a visitor, in the city where you live.

New Destiny is the largest provider of supportive housing for domestic violence survivors in New York and is a leading advocate in the effort to obtain the resources needed to end family homelessness in New York City.

General Description

The Director of Financial Resilience is a new position, created to launch and lead a department and team that assists domestic violence survivors in achieving financial stability, safety, and long-term wealth growth. This position will guide a team of three financial coaches, shape trauma-informed programming, and build partnerships with financial institutions and community organizations that expand access to resources for survivors. The Director will create a new department that will integrate a financial resilience model across New Destiny’s housing programs, with the goal of increasing the number of domestic violence survivors able to receive financial stabilization services, deepen survivors’ financial literacy and knowledge, and grow survivors’ financial health and wellness for long-term stability. This work is rooted in trauma-informed care and tailored to the experience and needs of the formerly homeless domestic violence survivors we serve.

Duties and Responsibilities

Design, implement, and evaluate financial empowerment programs, including coaching, credit repair, savings programs, asset building, debt management, and banking access.
Create curriculum for financial education and workshops and short-term financial coaching to stabilize and strengthen the economic health of survivor-led households.
Build out and execute policies and protocols for this new department, ensuring that all services being built out are survivor-centered, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive.
Develop key performance indicators to track outcomes and report to leadership and funders.
Supervise and support three financial coaches, including one-on-one supervision and performance reviews.
Provide access to training to financial coaches, including best practices and recovery from financial abuse.
Build and maintain relationships internally across departments and externally with banks, credit unions, and other financial institutions to create survivor-friendly products and services.
Partner with community organizations focusing on income security, financial independence and growth, including legal partners, eviction-prevention organizations, workforce development opportunities, and other social services to create seamless referral pathways.
Identify and pursue opportunities for matched savings and other wealth-building initiatives.
Manage program budget and ensure compliance with funder requirements.

Qualifications

A master’s degree in social work, finance, non-profit management, or a related field or equivalent experience is required.
Eight to ten years of work experience with at least three to five years in financial empowerment in a social services setting is required.
Three to five years in a supervisory role required.
Must have extensive knowledge of domestic violence dynamics and economic abuse, with experience working with trauma-informed care practices.
Experience working in or with the affordable housing industry, especially direct work with eviction prevention, preferred.
Must be a self-starter with experience in program development.
Proven success building partnerships with financial institutions and community organizations.
Must be a team player with strong communication, leadership, and data-tracking skills.
Financial coaching certifications strongly preferred (e.g., AFCPE, CFEC).
Bilingual in Spanish strongly preferred.

Compensation/Benefits

$100,000 a year with competitive benefits. This is a full-time position with a benefits package including medical, dental, vision, short disability, PTO paid holidays and 401(k). EOE

New Destiny is an equal opportunity employer and committed to diversity. Survivors of domestic violence and people who have experienced housing instability are encouraged to apply.

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

The Ministry of Energy and Minerals is responsible for sustaining the interests of Albertans through the stewardship and responsible development of energy and mineral resource systems.

Please review Energy and Minerals to learn more and what it has to offer.

The Strategy and Market Access (SAMA) Division is responsible for developing Alberta's strategic direction to deliver on energy mandates including natural gas infrastructure development, market access, energy market diversification, strategic foresight, economic analysis, and stakeholder engagement.

The Energy Futures Branch leads the development and implementation of strategies related to natural gas infrastructure, value-add initiatives, export opportunities including liquefied natural gas (LNG) and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), critical minerals, emerging resources, and pipeline regulatory processes

The Unit of Emerging Resources is responsible for strategy development and implementation of Alberta’s critical minerals and geo-thermal resources.

Role Responsibilities

Are you a strategic thinker and collaborative leader? Energy Futures is looking for a Director, Emerging Resources to provide strategic leadership and advance Alberta’s critical minerals, geothermal energy, and other emerging resource opportunities.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Energy Futures, this position provides strategic leadership for the Department’s mandated initiatives related to critical minerals, geothermal and other emerging opportunities. The position leads professional teams responsible for strategy and legislative development, complex projects, and work across government and with external partners to advance complex policy, investment, regulatory, and market priorities.

In This Role, You Will

Provide strategic advice, analysis and recommendations, for policies, programs, and initiatives related to critical minerals, geothermal energy, and other emerging resources.
Lead strategy planning, legislative and regulatory development, implementation planning and evaluation for Alberta’s Critical Minerals Strategy and Action Plan and other emerging resource development initiatives.
Direct the preparation of decision documents, briefing notes, correspondence, cabinet and Treasury Board materials, key messages and other executive products.
Lead complex, cross-ministry and cross-jurisdictional initiatives including engagement with federal, provincial and territorial partnerships on critical minerals.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with federal counterparts and industry to advance Alberta’s interests and strategic outcomes on critical minerals and other emerging opportunities. Lead, coach, and develop managers and staff while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and results-oriented work environment.
Identify opportunities to strengthen Alberta’s competitiveness, attract investment, and support mineral exploration, development, processing, and value-added opportunities.
Direct complex policy, economic, technical, regulatory, and market analysis and provide evidence-based recommendations to senior and executive leadership.
Represent the department on intergovernmental committees, working groups, industry forums, and other strategic initiatives.
Lead unit operations, workforce planning, financial oversights, priority setting, staff development, issues management and coordination oversight and continuous improvement while managing competing priorities and emerging issues.

This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic and collaborative leader to influence Alberta’s energy and mineral future. Your leadership will help shape policies, strengthen partnerships, attract investment, and advance the responsible development of Alberta’s emerging resources.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Systems Thinking: You will consider the broader economic, regulatory, competitive, and market environment when developing strategies for critical minerals, geothermal energy, and emerging resources.
Build Collaborative Environments: You will build strategic relationships with industry, Indigenous organizations, regulators, other governments, and cross-ministry partners to advance emerging resource priorities.
Develop Self and Others: You will provide clear direction, coaching, and mentorship to managers and staff, empowering your team to deliver on complex priorities. This aligns with the APS emphasis on achieving results through others and setting clear expectations.
Creative Problem Solving: You will analyze complex policy, economic, regulatory, and market issues and develop practical, evidence-based options and recommendations for senior leadership.
Drive for Results: You will establish clear priorities and lead the delivery of high-profile strategic initiatives while balancing competing priorities and maintaining accountability for results.
Agility: You will anticipate and respond to emerging issues, changing government priorities, and evolving energy and mineral markets while providing timely strategic advice.

Qualifications

University graduation in Public Administration, Business Administration, Economics, Engineering, Science, or a related field, supplemented by seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience required in Leading complex strategic initiatives, and issues management

Related experience or education may be considered as an equivalency on a one for one basis

Assets

Knowledge of Alberta, North American and global energy landscape.
Experience with investment attraction, market development, or resource competitiveness.
Experience working with industry, Indigenous organizations, governments, regulators, international investors or other strategic partners.
Experience managing human and financial resources and leading organisational change.
Advanced writing, briefing, engagement and presentation skills.
Ability to brief and present to senior leaders and Ministers.
Demonstrated ability to develop strategies, legislation, regulations and government decision documents such as cabinet reports.
Strong policial and financial acumen.

WOW 1 DAY PAINTING is at a pivotal point in its growth. We've just completed a brand refresh that launches across North America in Q1 2027, and we're looking for a Vice President, Marketing to make it a main driver of growth. Our goals are aggressive: double the business in the next three years, on the path to $100 million in system-wide revenue and a brand that triples in size over five to six years. This is a growth leadership role, not a traditional marketing role: you'll own business outcomes, not just marketing activities, and sit on the leadership team that decides how a franchise brand wins customers and new franchise partners.

About

We'll grow by going deeper in the markets we serve and by expanding into new ones through additional franchises, across residential and commercial (B2B) customers, with the mix expected to move toward about 60% residential and 40% commercial. You will:

Brand Relaunch & Digital Strategy

Lead the Q1 2027 North American launch of the refreshed brand and relaunched website.
Build the brand through video and digital content, resetting the digital strategy across paid, earned, shared, and owned (PESO) channels.
Build an internal content production capability alongside vendor partners.

Full-Funnel Customer Growth & Retention

Design, develop and manage a full-funnel growth strategy connecting customer acquisition, retention, and lifetime value across brand, performance, referral, and loyalty marketing.
Drive performance marketing, with a focus on Meta and YouTube.
Expand the referral program by leveraging an industry-leading customer experience.

Franchise Expansion & Local Execution

Lead franchise development marketing to attract new franchise partners and expand across North America.
Balance national brand strategy with local execution by planning and running marketing alongside franchise partners to grow leads, customers, revenue, and franchisee profitability.

Commercial (B2B) & Residential Market Growth

Grow commercial (B2B) revenue alongside residential revenue with the leadership team, helping shift the business mix toward ~60% residential and 40% commercial.
Deepen presence in existing markets while expanding into new territories.

Analytics, Operations & Team Leadership

Own measurement, attribution, and AI-enabled marketing operations.
Establish clear KPIs and scorecards to hold agencies, franchise partners, and the internal team accountable for results.
Build and lead a team of in-brand marketers and vendor partners.

This role is based in Vancouver or Toronto, with a hybrid work model.

About You

You're a customer- and partner-minded, full-funnel growth leader who combines strategic thinking with strong execution, builds accountable teams and partners, and knows how to scale both brand and performance across a franchise system. You bring:

10+ years in marketing, including 5+ years leading multiple marketing functions across multiple locations.
Proven full-funnel growth across paid, shared, owned channels including programs that turn customers into repeat business and advocates.
Multi-location and franchise systems expertise: you balance national brand strategy with local execution, franchisee engagement and profitability, and you know how to market to attract new franchise partners.
Brand building through video and digital content, with experience building an internal content production capability.
Performance marketing expertise, across all digital channels.
Measurement, attribution and AI-enabled marketing operations, with ownership of data and outcomes through KPIs, business scorecards (BSC), OKRs and agency oversight, and revenue operations experience (CRM, funnel, automation).
A commercial orientation: you turn business objectives into strategy, align people, technology, process and investment, and have grown B2B revenue alongside residential or consumer revenue.
Exceptional leadership, influence and communication: you build high-performing teams and create alignment and accountability across agencies, franchise partners and stakeholders.
A bachelor's degree in marketing, business or a related field (an MBA is an asset), and an understanding of CASL and CAN-SPAM.

The Brand

WOW 1 DAY PAINTING is a fast-growing house painting franchise and part of O2E Brands, the parent company of the hugely successful 1-800-GOT-JUNK?. Our franchise partners deliver an industry-leading customer experience, and we've just completed a brand refresh that launches across North America in Q1 2027, backed by the digital presence and the team to double the business in three years.

O2E Brands has been voted one of the Best Workplaces in Canada 15 times. When we say It's All About People, we mean it: our hybrid model helps us get together to collaborate, celebrate and connect, with flexibility where it makes sense for you.

What's In It For You

A seat on the leadership team and the chance to shape the growth of a brand.
Long-term incentive opportunities.
Salary Range: $160,000-190,000, plus bonus, plus profit share.
Extended health and dental, professional development programs, and wellness initiatives.

Join Us
